                                         PROSPECTUS 2025-26          2
  Baosi Banikanta Kakati College




Established in 1971, Baosi Banikanta Kakati College has proudly completed over 50 glorious years
of its journey in the field of higher education. Guided by the timeless mantra "Tamaso Ma
Jyotirgamaya"—a call to move from darkness to light—the college firmly believes in the
transformative power of education. It sees higher learning as a key driver of societal progress,
shaping students into confident, capable leaders for an ever-evolving world.
Set in the lap of nature, our verdant campus offers a peaceful and inspiring environment for learning.
The college is well-equipped with modern facilities, including state-of-the-art digital classrooms and
a fully air-conditioned library enriched with a wide range of Online Educational Resources (OER).
These amenities support both academic excellence and extracurricular engagement. We have also
signed numerous Memorandums of Understanding (MoUs) with educational and non-educational
institutions to promote collaborative learning and knowledge exchange.
In the academic session 2020–21, we introduced a Postgraduate course in Assamese, offering 20 seats
and consistently producing commendable results. Plans are also underway to launch a Postgraduate
program in English. Our Bachelor of Computer Applications (BCA) program has been accredited by
the All India Council for Technical Education (AICTE), a mark of quality and rigor.
We take immense pride in our strong and supportive community, which includes retired faculty
members, alumni, parents, the Rash Committee, and our neighboring localities. Together, we strive
for excellence not only in academics but also in sports, cultural pursuits, and research. To enrich
student life further, we have introduced a variety of value-added programs such as a Certificate
Course in Yoga, Kung Fu training, and other skill-building initiatives. The college also offers
departmental certificate courses and 20 additional free courses under PMKVY 5.0 and the IIT
Bombay Spoken Tutorial project.
Since the 2023–24 academic year, the college has adopted the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020
curriculum under Gauhati University. From 2024–25 onward, as per the directive of the Hon’ble
Governor of Assam, NEP-based programs will be implemented under Bhattadev University. These
forward-looking regulations are designed to provide flexibility through the Choice Based Credit
System (CBCS), multiple entry and exit options, and the Academic Bank of Credit—creating a more
student-centric learning experience that fosters holistic development.
With these initiatives, Baosi Banikanta Kakati College reaffirms its commitment to nurturing young
minds for a brighter, more prosperous future. I warmly welcome all prospective students and
encourage you to make full use of the college’s academic and co-curricular resources. Together, let us
strive toward the collective vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.

                                                         PROSPECTUS 2025-26                      3
  Baosi Banikanta Kakati College




F   ounded in 1971 through the tireless efforts of Late Mahendra Mohan
Choudhury—a distinguished freedom fighter and political leader—Baosi
Banikanta Kakati College stands as a testament to Assam’s rich cultural and
educational heritage. Named after Dr. Banikanta Kakati, a renowned scholar
and academician, the college embodies the fusion of local identity with a
commitment to academic excellence.
Nestled amidst the tranquil landscapes of Baosi, away from the urban bustle
of Barpeta town, the college has long served as a beacon of higher education
for the rural communities of Lower Assam. For over five decades, it has
continued to attract students with aspirations for quality education, building a
proud legacy of academic distinction.
Today, Baosi Banikanta Kakati College supports a vibrant community of
around 1,800 students across a range of disciplines, including Arts, Science,
and Computer Applications at the Higher Secondary and Undergraduate
levels. The college has been accredited by NAAC, Bangalore with a "B"
grade in its third cycle of assessment and accreditation. Our tradition of
academic excellence is reflected in the growing number of First Class
graduates and University rank holders, with the overall pass percentage
consistently exceeding the University average.
Staying true to its mission of inclusivity and social responsibility, the college
provides stipends to students from economically disadvantaged backgrounds,
marginalized communities, and remote areas. Modern facilities such as
separate RCC hostels for male and female students, and a well-resourced
library further enhance the learning environment, supporting both academic
and personal growth.
Guided by the motto "Search for Talent and Its Nurturing," Baosi Banikanta
Kakati College is deeply committed to discovering and fostering the potential
of every student, regardless of background. The college remains steadfast in
its responsibility to serve not only its students but also the wider community.
Through its enduring dedication to academic excellence, inclusivity, and
social empowerment, Baosi Banikanta Kakati College continues to inspire
and shape future generations, playing a vital role in advancing the educational
landscape of Assam.

  NEP 2020 based FYUGP Curriculum under Bhattadev
  University
  Following the order of the Honourable Governor of Assam, B.B.K,
  College has been affiliated under the Bhattadev University from the
  academic session 2024-25. The college follows the NEP 2020 based
  curriculum framed by the Bhattadev University and offers FUYGP
  with the options mentioned below:
  ✓ Students who opt to exit after completion of the first year and
     have secured 40 credits will be awarded a certificate if, in addition,
     they complete one vocational course of 4 credits during the
     summer vacation of the first year.
  ✓ Students who opt to exit after completion of the second year and
     have secured 80 credits will be awarded the diploma if, in
     addition, they complete one vocational course of 4 credits during
     the summer vacation of the second year.
  ✓ Students who opt to exit after completion of the third year and
     have secured 120 credits will be eligible for the bachelor in the
     major discipline without honours.
  ✓ Students after completion of the fourth year and have secured 160
     credits will be eligible for the bachelor with honours in the major
     discipline.
  ✓ Students are allowed to re-enter the programme within three
     years and complete the programme within the stipulated
     maximum period of seven years.

 Outline of Courses:
 The broad categories of courses and minimum credits
 required for the 4-year Honours s as per the UGC document
 are as follows:
 1. Major (Core) course/paper: 80 credits
 2. Minor course/paper: 32 credits
 3. Interdisciplinary course/paper (IDC): 9 credits
 4. Ability Enhancement Course/paper (AEC): 8 credits
 5. Skill Enhancement Course/paper (SEC): 9 credits
 6. Value Added Course/paper (VAC): 8 credits
 7. Summer Internship: 2 credits
 8. Research Project/ Dissertation: 12 credits (for Honours
 with Research )

 The following points may be noted:
 • In lieu of the Research Project, a student may study 3 courses each
 of 4 credits (i.e. total 12 credits), leading to an Honours (without
 Research).
 • For the 4-year Honours s the Major subject/ discipline requires 80
 credits and the . Minor subject/ discipline requires 32 credits.
 • For a Double Major, the minimum credit requirements are 48 (3-
 year ) and 60 (4- year Honours ) respectively in a subject/ discipline
 other than the original Major.
 • In the UGC framework, papers in Major and Minor disciplines are
 categorized into levels of 100, 200, 300 and 400. Therefore, a course
 (paper) offered by a Department, say with 4 credits and of level 200,
 may be taken both as a Major (Core) course by one student and as a
 Minor course by another student having a different Major discipline,
 possibly in different semesters.

  Some Important terms
  Credit: A unit by which the course work is measured. It determines the
  number of hours of instructions required per week.
  Theory/Tutorial classes: 1 credit = 1 hour / week, and
  Practical classes: 1 credit = 2 hours / week
  Credit Point: It is the product of grade point and number of credits for a
  course.
  Letter Grade: It is an index of the performance of students in a said
  course.
  Grade Point: It is a numerical weight allotted to each letter grade on a
  certain point scale.
  The following table explains the above two points
       Letter Grade             Grade Point               Performane
              O                       10                  Outstanding
             A+                        9                   Excellent
              A                        8                  Very Good
             B+                        7                     Good
              B                        6                Above Average
             C+                        5                    Average
              C                        4                      Pass
              F                        0                      Fail
              I                        0              Absent/Incomplete

  EXAMINATION RULES AND EVALUATION PROCESS
 Evaluation is an integral component of education system and the college
 always devise such an evaluation mechanism, which is not only time bound
 but also transparent.
 Examination Rules for H.S. Examinations
 To evaluate students’ learning level, the college adopts continuous internal
 evaluation even at H.S. level for capacity development of students. At higher
 secondary level, there will be periodical class test, and a unit test
 examination. In addition, the students of HS 2nd year must appear in a test
 examination. Based on this, students will be allowed to fill up the forms of
 final examinations held by AHSEC. The final examinations will be held as per
 the guidelines of AHSEC.
 Examination Rules NEP 2020 based FYUGP System :
 Evaluation under FYUGP system consists of both internal and external
 evaluation. Internal evaluation has the following component-
 - attendance mark (for details visit https://bbkcollege.co.in/exam.php)
 - sessional examination
 - Home assignment
 - Group discussion/ Seminars/Quiz, etc.
 External evaluation is held as per the guidelines of the affiliating University
 and it is displayed in the college website in due course of time.

 Important Points (For all):
 ➢ In case of any dispute regarding evaluation or unforeseen events, the
    matter may be placed before the Academic Committee for amicable
    settlement.
 ➢ The rules of examination and evaluation of students are as per the
    examination and evaluation rules of Gauhati University and Bhattadev
    University, which is available at the official website of Gauhati
    University, Bhattadev University and B.B.K. College.
 ➢ Students unable to appear in a test on medical grounds must submit
    application along with medical certificates prior to the test. Under no
    circumstances, medical certificates will be entertained in more than one
    test.

    website/ college notice board from time to time to update them on
    examination guidelines and schedule.

The College has an excellent Library and Information Centre, one of the
institution's central support services. The library has been carefully designed to
provide a comfortable seating and reading environment with proper light and air
conditioners. It's a spacious premise comprising an area of 2795 sq feet. The
library has the capacity of sitting more than 70 readers in total with the provision
of separate reading rooms for students and teachers. There is also a dedicated
digital room for accessing e-documents & internet in the library and a beautifully
designed periodical section with group discussion tables.
The library has a boasting collection of more than 16000 physical books and
other resources. Currently, the library is subscribing to one peer-reviewed journal
in physical format, 8 Magazines and 3 Newspapers. The library also preserves
some valuable old and rare manuscripts collected from the localities. The library
is subscribing to N-List & NDLi services which provides free access to more than 2
lacs e-books and 6000 e-journals. The Library has its own Digital Library over

collected by the college.

operated through the software using barcode printed ID Card. The library has its
own OPAC for catalogue searching, Online Attendance system and a dedicated
webpage. To enhance security, the library is equipped with CCTV system. The
library provides reprographic services to the students. As part of the automation
and digitization, the library has a tabletop scanner for the digitization process.

automation purpose.
